messages:
kai: spinning up an avalon11b int4 canary on dedicated pool. seeing allocator churn and a small QA regression on long-generation prompts. tagging y'all.
mira: can you paste the canary runtime config and a representative log snippet?
kai: runtime config for canary:
```
model: avalon11b
quant: int4
prefetch: true
kv_prefetch_slots: 24
max_new_tokens: 600
batch_size: 5
streaming: true
```
kai: recent noisy logs (abridged):
```
[2026-03-21T02:17:02Z] WARN evictor: evict slots=3 reason=frag_threshold
[2026-03-21T02:17:03Z] WARN allocator: fallback_alloc count=9 size=900MiB
[2026-03-21T02:17:03Z] ERROR runtime: request failed status=RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
```
sam: those fallback_alloc spikes + multiple small evictions smell like over-prefetch with int4. what QA signal moved?
mira: qa: longform rouge-l down ~1.6%, qa-f1 down 1.2% on prompts that generate >350 tokens. also increase in token repetition.
ania: first-pass hypotheses:
- int4 quant + prefetch causes fragmented allocations when kv cache grows for long gens
- large max_new_tokens amplifies transient memory working set
- batch_size 5 -> tail latency/gen overlap causes concurrent allocator pressure
ania: quick experiments to isolate:
- set prefetch=false (turn off eager KV pulls)
- shrink max_new_tokens to 256 for canary traffic
- drop batch_size to 2 or enable microbatching for big requests
- enable kv_trim on tail and lower kv_prefetch_slots
- add sanity eval runs with fixed RNG seeds
mira: adding: run a quality-only ablation where we keep int4 but revert prefetch=false and keep max_new_tokens=600 to see if prefetch affects quality directly.
kai: I'll push a canary change: prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=256, batch_size=2. Also add a reactive fallback: if fallback_alloc > 6/min then fallback to int8 for that worker.
infra-bot: deploy started by kai on pool:dedicated-canary-3 (deploy_id: dpl_20260321_002)
sanity-bot: scheduled: eval/avalon11b/canary/2026-03-21/sha=b1c7 trigger by @kai
sam: in parallel i'll run mem sweeps across int4 vs int8 with prefetch on/off and capture slab histograms + allocator flamegraphs. ping me when the canary is up.
kai: deploy live. initial telemetry: evictions dropped from ~12/min to ~2/min, fallback_alloc events down to 1/min. posting snapshot in ~20m.
mira: kicked off the quality-only ablation (int4 + prefetch=false + max_new_tokens=600). linking: https://go.redwood/evals/avalon11b/b1c7
ania: visualization note: allocation skew is concentrated in small-slab classes (64-512B) during tail of generation. suggests many small KV expansion/compact ops.
sam: mem-sweep early results: int4+prefs on = worst fragmentation; int8 reduces fallback_alloc by ~70% and repetition decreases slightly. interestingly int4+prefs off looks close to int8 on quality but with slightly higher latency.
mira: quality ablation partial: prefetch=false but still int4 & max_new_tokens=600 -> rouge/qa-f1 almost recovered (delta ~0.3%). so prefetch was a major factor for quality regressions.
kai: conclusion so far: prefetch aggressively with int4 on long gens causes allocator churn -> eviction patterns -> degraded generation (repeat/truncate). Plan:
1) default canary config -> prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=256, batch_size=2 (rolled)
2) lifecycle: gradual rollout with telemetry gating (evictions, fallback_alloc, rouge/qa-f1)
3) longer-term: evaluate mixed-precision per-key (keep some KV in int8) and/or adaptive prefetch (disable for requests expected >256 tokens)
4) add a runtime telemetry alert if fallback_alloc > 5/min OR evictions > 5/min for a worker -> auto-fallback to int8
5) create an eval test harness with deterministic seeds and longform prompts for onboarding regressions
mira: agree. I'll merge the eval harness prompts into onboarding CI.
ania: i'll add a dashboard tile: slab histogram + kv_evictions + allocation flamegraph per worker.
sam: i'll prototype mixed-int8-for-keys patch next sprint; for now safe defaults look good.
kai: thanks everyone. i'll keep the thread updated with final 24h diffs. :thumbsup:
